sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx:Quality Checks row 51 (check 50); Internal Quality Checks row 51
.qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/task: recursive filesystem inventory, including hidden entries
evidence: The workbook's Quality Checks row 51/check 50 requires a closed task directory. The frozen skill reference staged-task-contract.md:32 explicitly lists `node_modules` under 'Must be absent'; quality-checks.md:200-202 requires checking for committed caches and build residue. Recursive filesystem inspection of the frozen task found solution/app/node_modules/ containing 1,550 files and 74,696,504 bytes, including node_modules/.package-lock.json, node_modules/.bin/acorn.cmd and node_modules/react/package.json. This is a real installed dependency tree, not the skill's known coverage.json or seed_data.json false positive. The required staged roots and test files are present, and environment/assets/seed_data.json is allowed by the closed list. The prebuilt solution/app/public assets are used by server.js:130-131 and referenced by public/index.html; they are necessary to the runnable golden app and are not the defect. solution/solve.sh:38 executes `cp -a "$source_app/." /app/`, so the unwanted dependency tree is copied into the installed golden app. No runtime run was needed to establish the folder-content defect; raw-evidence-index.json was absent when checked.
counterexample: A task package can contain an otherwise working golden app plus the 1,550 installed node_modules files; a check that lists only Git-tracked or rg-visible files would miss the directory and wrongly pass this closed-folder row. A conforming package may include the compiled public assets that server.js serves and the required seed_data.json, so rejecting those as stray files would wrongly fail it.
suggested_fix: Remove solution/app/node_modules from the task source and frozen deliverable, keep package.json/package-lock.json and the served public assets, then create a new candidate and verify the golden app installs and runs with its intended dependencies.
